subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw support cross-gateway `sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn` through ad hoc `gateway.peers` and raw tool `gatewayUrl` parameters, or should this wait for a narrower federation/bridge protocol design?
rationale: This is a new remote execution and session-state boundary; code review can identify defects, but only maintainers can choose the permanent auth/addressing model and acceptable blast radius.

options.title: Require federation design first
options.body: Pause this PR and use the linked cross-gateway issues to define the bridge protocol, identity, operator scopes, and proof bar before code lands.

options.title: Narrow to configured peers only
options.body: Remove raw `gatewayUrl` tool parameters and redesign named peers around explicit allowlisting, credentials, tests, docs, and live proof on current main.

options.title: Accept ad hoc peer routing
options.body: Allow this feature direction only with explicit security-owner approval, fixed protocol defects, rebase, and real two-gateway proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Require federation design first
recommendation.body: Pause this PR and use the linked cross-gateway issues to define the bridge protocol, identity, operator scopes, and proof bar before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the deepest history across session tools, gateway routing, and security-sensitive session visibility changes.
